# Generate unique profile pictures for social media with Midjourney

> **In short:** Midjourney is an AI image generator. In this guide you use it inside Discord: you type /imagine with a short description, get four options, pick one, and save it as your new profile picture. You need a Midjourney subscription.

A profile picture is often the first thing people see about you online. With Midjourney you can describe the look you want, such as a cartoon portrait or a watercolor avatar, and get several versions in about a minute. This guide uses Midjourney's Discord bot. You can also create on the Midjourney website; Midjourney's own docs explain both.

## Before you start

- **A Midjourney subscription.** Midjourney's Discord Quick Start says you need a subscription before you can create images. Check the plans on [midjourney.com](https://www.midjourney.com).
- **A Discord account** and the Discord app or website.
- **About 15–20 minutes** for your first few tries.

## Step 1: Join the Midjourney server on Discord

Open Discord and find the server list on the left side. Press the **+** button at the bottom of the list, click **Join a Server**, then paste the official invite link `http://discord.gg/midjourney` and press **Join**.

Then open a channel where the bot works. Midjourney's docs say to use any channel labeled **general-#** or **newbie-1** through **newbie-10**. The bot does not generate images in other channels on its server.

You'll know it worked when the Midjourney server appears in your server list and you can open one of those channels.

## Step 2: Start your first image with /imagine

A **prompt** is the text description you give the AI. Type **/** in the message box, and a list of commands appears. Keep typing until you see **/imagine**, click it, type your description into the prompt field, and press **Enter**. The first time, the Midjourney Bot asks you to accept its Terms of Service before it creates anything.

💬 Example: `/imagine prompt: a cheerful fox wearing round glasses, cartoon style, bright colors`

You'll know it worked when the bot starts working on your request. Midjourney says it creates four image options within a minute. If you don't see any Midjourney commands, check Midjourney's command troubleshooting tips.

## Step 3: Write a prompt for a profile picture

Be specific about the subject, mood, style, colors, and background. Words like "portrait," "headshot," or "close-up" help keep the focus on one face. Midjourney's docs say images use a square 1:1 aspect ratio by default, which suits most profile picture slots. If you have changed your default settings, add `--ar 1:1` at the end of the prompt to keep the image square.

💬 Example: `/imagine prompt: [describe the person or character], smiling gently, digital art portrait, soft pastel colors, simple background --ar 1:1`

You'll know it worked when your prompt includes who or what is in the picture, a style, and a simple background.

## Step 4: Review your grid of four images

You'll get a grid of four images with two rows of buttons under it:

- **U1, U2, U3, U4** separate one image from the grid, so it's easier to download and edit. In current Midjourney versions, these buttons no longer make the image bigger.
- **V1, V2, V3, V4** create a new grid of variations based on one image.
- The **🔄** button reruns your prompt for a fresh grid.

The numbers follow the grid: 1 is top left, 2 is top right, 3 is bottom left, and 4 is bottom right.

You'll know it worked when you can see the grid and both rows of buttons.

## Step 5: Pick your favorite and adjust it

Click the **U** button for the image you like best. Once it is separated, more options appear, including **Vary (Strong)** and **Vary (Subtle)** for new versions, **Zoom Out** to extend the background, the arrow buttons to extend the image in one direction, and **Web** to open the image on midjourney.com. If you want it larger, Midjourney's docs describe **Upscale (Subtle)**, which keeps the look close to the original, and **Upscale (Creative)**, which adds new details. Upscaling uses more of your subscription's GPU time.

You'll know it worked when a single image of your choice appears with the extra buttons below it.

## Step 6: Save your new profile picture

Midjourney's docs say: on a computer, click the image to open it at full size, then right-click and choose **Save image**. On a phone, long-tap the image and then tap the download icon. Your images are also available on midjourney.com when you log in with your Discord account.

You'll know it worked when the image file opens in your photos or files app.

## Step 7: Refine or try again

If the result isn't quite right, try **Vary (Subtle)** for small changes, or write a new /imagine prompt with clearer details. Midjourney also has **Vary Region** in Discord for regenerating one part of an image. Small, step-by-step changes to your wording usually work better than starting over every time.

You'll know it worked when a new version gets closer to the picture you have in mind.

## Common mistakes

- **A vague prompt.** "Person" gives a very generic result. *The fix:* Describe the face, expression, clothing, style, and background.
- **Using the wrong channel.** On the Midjourney server, the bot only works in its general and newbie channels. *The fix:* Use a **general-#** or **newbie-1** to **newbie-10** channel.
- **Expecting U buttons to enlarge the image.** In current versions they only separate the image. *The fix:* Use **Upscale (Subtle)** or **Upscale (Creative)** when you really need a bigger file.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can make a profile picture or avatar that matches your personality, without needing a photo shoot.
- **For your business or work:** You can create a consistent illustrated look for a small team or project page. Check your workplace's rules on AI images first.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a cartoon or illustrated style. It is easier to get a pleasing result than with a realistic portrait.

## Try it now

Open Discord, go to a **newbie** channel on the Midjourney server, and type: `/imagine prompt: a friendly astronaut with a big smile, cartoon style, bright colors`. Pick your favorite with a U button and save it.
